topics.title: Barter exchange and the functions of money

concepts.learning_objective: Explain barter exchange and why the double coincidence of wants makes it costly in a large economy.
Describe money as a medium of exchange and a unit of account and use it to work out relative prices.
Explain money as a store of value and how a rising price level erodes its purchasing power.

topics.title: Demand for money: income, interest and the transaction motive

concepts.learning_objective: State how the demand for money depends on income and on the rate of interest.
Calculate and interpret the transaction demand for money using MdT = kT and MdT = kPY.
Calculate the velocity of circulation of money and relate it to k.

topics.title: Speculative demand for money, bond prices and the liquidity trap

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using present value, why the price of a bond is inversely related to the market rate of interest.
Explain why the speculative demand for money is inversely related to the rate of interest.
Describe the liquidity trap and why extra money then fails to lower the rate of interest.
Identify the functions of the central bank and the meaning of high-powered money.
Explain how commercial banks accept deposits, lend part of them and earn the spread, as in Lala's story.

topics.title: Money creation by the banking system and the money multiplier

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the assets, liabilities and net worth of a bank's balance sheet.
Explain how the Cash Reserve Ratio limits the loans a bank can make in each round.
Calculate the money multiplier and the deposits and loans created from a given amount of reserves.

topics.title: Policy tools to control money supply

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the central bank is called the lender of last resort.
Distinguish quantitative and qualitative tools of monetary control and the effect of the bank rate.
Explain outright open market operations, repo and reverse repo and their effect on money supply.

topics.title: Measures of money supply, fiat money and demonetisation
topics.ncert_sections: The supply of money: various measures; Box 3.2

concepts.learning_objective: Define fiat money and legal tender and explain why demand deposits are not legal tender.
State and calculate M1, M2, M3 and M4 and rank them by liquidity.
Evaluate the effects of the 2016 demonetisation on the economy and the banking system.
